dimension: Scientific tutorials and examples (benchmark section 4, priority 4)
already_met: Delegation principle is already in place: content/guides/using-apps.md ('Find the app's own documentation') says 'What an app does, and what its notebooks expect, is described there, not on this site', and pages_apps.using_section (scripts/lcsite/pages_apps.py:108-120) links to docs_url or the app README. The site does not duplicate app-specific instructions, which is exactly what benchmark section 4 asks.

The manifest schema already has optional `quickstart` (<=6 plain-text steps, rendered as an <ol> in 'Using it'), `docs_url`, `screenshots` (caption doubles as alt), `doi`, so the wiring point exists and `optional_list`/`in` handling is in place (but see gap 1: no one uses it).

NucleiSky (CellMigrationLab/NucleiSky@main docs/) meets 6 of 8 items: preparation (docs/2D/data_preparation.md, 3D/data_preparation.md: formats, pixel size, header inspection), parameters (docs/2D/workflow.md, matchers.md, api.md), expected output (docs/exports.md: file tree, 'aligned_on_full_px.tif', transform JSON; docs/qc.md 'Accept / Investigate / Reject' with baseline pass criteria and panel-by-panel reading guide), interpretation (docs/qc.md 'Metric Interpretation Guide'), limitations (docs/limitations.md: similarity-only model, >=10 nuclei, repetitive tissue, anisotropy; README 'Two Golden Rules'), transfer to own data (workflow.md 'Reuse the saved transform'). Reproducibility: DOI in manifest and README citation, per-notebook CHANGELOG, environment pinned (docs/installation.md: Python 3.12.13).

CellTracksColab has built-in example data wired into the notebook: a 'Use test dataset' checkbox (default True in CellTracksColab_TrackMate.ipynb, 1.2 cell) downloads Zenodo record 8413510 (T_cell_dataset.zip, 373 MB, TrackMate CSV, verified via the Zenodo API); README 'Resources' also lists record 8420011 (CellTracksColab-format, 364 MB, CC-BY-4.0). Notebook sections have per-step explanations, a QC part (5.1 balance, 5.2 similarity) and a Version log; README states 'does not yet support track merging or splitting'.

GuessTheCondition (CellMigrationLab/GuessTheCondition@main README.md) is the best-documented app: 'Prepare your images' (folder layout, .tif/.tiff, channels, z-stacks), a built-in 'Create a demo experiment' tool (src/guessthecondition/demo.py: 2 conditions x 3 repeats, 128 x 128 uint16, seed=0, so deterministic), 'How the results are read' (replicate = biological repeat, chance definition, tick/warning symbols, honest handling of 1-2 repeats), and a notebook GuessTheCondition_API_Example that runs a whole game with a simulated player.

LabConstrictor-Playground (section: testing) is honest and self-contained: README 'Reading the answer' table (tick / warning / cross with what to do), 'Honest limits' paragraph, 'Make test data' tool with seeded synthetic files (3-channel image with channel means 10/20/30, labels, time-lapse, points). It is a diagnostic app, so the scientific-example requirement does not apply to it.

Build-side of the Use track hands off correctly in tone: the install, open and troubleshooting guides are task-ordered; the hub picture of the Welcome notebook matches what the template builds. The Welcome notebook is a launcher and update checker only (.tools/templates/Welcome_template.ipynb: notebook table + 'Check for Updates'); it correctly does not pretend to be a tutorial, and its Description column is fed by each notebook's requirements.yaml `description`, which is the right owner (the app).
